description:
Trinity College, a research university in Dublin, was founded in 1592 by Queen Elizabeth I based on the universities of Oxford and Cambridge. Considered one of Europe's outstanding universities, Trinity College is also called Ireland's most prestigious university. Trinity College's library is the largest in Ireland. Although the school is best known for its achievements in law, literature, and the humanities, it also conducts large-scale research in the fields of nanotechnology, engineering, politics, psychology, and English. Trinity currently has more than 18,000 students, 24% of whom are foreign nationals. In addition, with its 47-acre campus in the heart of Dublin, the school is close to many museums, theatres, restaurants, and historical sites. The success of undergraduate and graduate programs in Ireland has been proven worldwide. Trinity College, which was the first Irish school to be among the top 50 universities in 2009, is now the 101st university in the world according to the QS World University Ranking.

Trinity College Dublin offers accommodations in three locations throughout the city, all of which are either near the campus or are on campus itself. On-campus housing is located in either the historic buildings in the center of the campus or in more modern developments further east. At Trinity Hall, Dartry, the majority of the accommodation is in modern purpose-built blocks near Rathmines in Dublin 6 and is a short cycle or public transport journey from the campus. The last accommodation is Kavanagh Court in Dublin 1 which is less than a 15-minute walk from Trinity. This private accommodation is fully immersed in the Trinity community and offers the best available options for student accommodation in the city.
